generator_provenance.generation_method: Semantic situations were authored from G3 first and then encoded only with the public fact keys and public violation-code vocabulary for each primary requirement.

cases.rationale: An external baseline may be legitimate even when its backend revision cannot be pinned, provided the unknown/unavailable revision and resulting reproducibility limitation are recorded and no exact-version claim is made.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid external service with unavailable immutable backend revision; tests that explicit limitation disclosure is not over-rejected.

cases.rationale: Claiming an exact immutable version while the backend revision is unknown contradicts the stable-identity/version requirement, even when the reproducibility limitation is otherwise disclosed.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Contradictory exact-pinning claim in the presence of explicitly unknown revision state.

cases.rationale: A post-protected baseline change is allowed only as successor evidence with the original result preserved and Task 7 lineage semantics applied; it must not rewrite the earlier comparison.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate post-protected baseline evolution with full historical preservation and successor lineage.

cases.rationale: A material baseline change after protected inspection cannot be folded into the original evidence; successor evidence is required even if the earlier result and lineage are preserved.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Post-protected modification that preserves history but silently lacks successor evidence.

cases.rationale: The strongest-applicable claim is bounded to a predeclared search contract whose scope and cutoff are fixed before protected outcomes, with considered comparators and exclusions preserved.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Bounded strongest-applicable selection that explicitly avoids any claim of global optimality.

cases.rationale: Using protected outcomes to decide comparator selection violates the predeclared strongest-applicable selection contract even when search scope, cutoff, and provenance are otherwise complete.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Outcome-dependent comparator selection hidden inside an otherwise well-documented search process.

cases.rationale: A simple diagnostic anchor may be beaten while the strongest comparator is not; that result is legitimate if it remains diagnostic and is not reported as general superiority.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Favorable anchor result coexisting with an unfavorable stronger-comparator result without claim inflation.

cases.rationale: A favorable result against a diagnostic anchor cannot stand in for failure against the stronger comparator required by the claim.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Diagnostic anchor is promoted into claim-bearing evidence despite failure against the strongest comparator.

cases.rationale: Both sides may legitimately receive warmed persistent information when the transcript and retrieval state are materially matched; fairness requires parity, not necessarily a cold start.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid warmed-state comparison with equal persistent information on both sides.

cases.rationale: Giving only the candidate materially useful prior transcript and warmed retrieval state creates an undeclared information advantage and violates information/opportunity parity.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Indirect persistent-state leakage through transcript and retrieval cache rather than the nominal task input.

cases.rationale: A mutable environment can support a valid comparison when drift is actively controlled through snapshotting, paired execution or replay and any residual limitation is explicitly qualified.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate evaluation in a mutable external environment with multiple redundant drift controls.

cases.rationale: When the environment can change over time, an unpaired, unsnapshotted, unreplayed comparison with no drift qualification cannot establish evaluation parity.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Temporal drift confound in an otherwise nominally identical comparison.

cases.rationale: A material asymmetry is legitimate when it is predeclared and is exactly the causal treatment the comparison claims to evaluate; fairness does not require identical algorithms.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Material but scientifically legitimate treatment asymmetry.

cases.rationale: Predeclaring an asymmetry does not make it valid when the asymmetry is unrelated to the scientific distinction being claimed and simply advantages one side.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Declared but causally irrelevant advantage masquerading as the treatment.

cases.rationale: Unequal manual iteration counts can be legitimate when the tuning policy is predeclared and the difference is scientifically justified rather than used to weaken the comparator.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid asymmetric tuning opportunity justified by the scientific design.

cases.rationale: Systematically giving the candidate more manual tuning iterations without scientific justification weakens comparison fairness even under a documented policy.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Quantified tuning-opportunity imbalance under an otherwise predeclared policy.

cases.rationale: Material provenance may be unavailable, but the field must remain explicit as UNAVAILABLE or UNKNOWN rather than being silently omitted or invented.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate explicit unavailable provenance rather than fabricated precision.

cases.rationale: When the evaluator revision is available, omitting that material provenance prevents faithful interpretation and replay of the comparison.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Known provenance is silently dropped despite being obtainable.

cases.rationale: An unpinned external API can be represented honestly as an irreproducible external dependency when the limitation is explicit; exact reconstruction is not required where the system cannot support it.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid irreproducible dependency with truthful reproducibility classification.

cases.rationale: An unpinned external dependency is incompatible with a claim of exact reconstruction even if the dependency limitation is separately noted.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Contradictory exact-reconstruction label for an unpinned external API.

cases.rationale: Stochastic replication is legitimate when stopping is governed in advance and repeated runs are not misrepresented as independent Task 7 evaluation units.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Valid repeated stochastic runs with preregistered stopping and no pseudoreplication claim.

cases.rationale: Continuing or stopping protected runs in response to favorable outcomes is outcome-driven optional stopping when no governing rule was preregistered.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Outcome-dependent stopping without pseudoreplication, isolating stopping governance.

cases.rationale: Effect uncertainty is valid when analysis respects Task 7 evaluation units and independence groups and does not inflate sample size by treating repeated seeds as new independent units.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Dependency-aware uncertainty analysis under repeated stochastic seeds.

cases.rationale: Repeated seeds from the same underlying evaluation units cannot be counted as independent scientific evidence merely because the executions differ.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Pseudoreplication introduced only at the statistical-analysis layer.

cases.rationale: A failed primary claim may coexist with reportable secondary findings, provided the primary failure remains explicit and no secondary measure is promoted post hoc into support for the original claim.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate negative primary result with secondary evidence kept in its preregistered role.

cases.rationale: Promoting a secondary measure after observing failure of the primary measure violates selective-reporting control even if the primary failure is still recorded.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Outcome-driven metric-role reassignment without erasing the failed primary result.

cases.rationale: A claim-affecting hard constraint is validly governed when frozen before protected inspection and independently capable of blocking PASS regardless of aggregate performance.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Hard-constraint gate kept separate from favorable aggregate metrics.

cases.rationale: A claim-affecting hard-constraint violation cannot be neutralized by a favorable mean, composite, or secondary metric once the constraint applies.
cases.adversarial_dimension: A predeclared hard constraint is improperly converted into a soft contribution to an aggregate.

cases.rationale: Benchmark sampling and weighting are legitimate when their rules are frozen before protected outcomes and the intended difficulty distribution is preserved.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Stable benchmark portfolio despite heterogeneous difficulty.

cases.rationale: Changing benchmark weights after protected outcomes can change the conclusion and violates the requirement to freeze conclusion-sensitive portfolio rules in advance.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Post-outcome weighting manipulation while leaving the nominal task set unchanged.

cases.rationale: A dynamically generated benchmark may have unknown contamination status; dynamism itself is not cleanliness evidence, and uncertainty may be represented explicitly.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid dynamic benchmark with contamination left UNKNOWN rather than assumed CLEAN.

cases.rationale: Declaring a dynamic benchmark clean solely because it is dynamically generated substitutes generation method for actual contamination evidence.
cases.adversarial_dimension: False cleanliness inference from benchmark dynamism in the absence of supporting provenance.

cases.rationale: A same-family evaluator can be claim-bearing when its identity, version, scoring, relationship, bias controls, and an appropriate alternative cross-check are all explicit.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid same-family judge with correlated-bias controls rather than automatic disqualification.

cases.rationale: When the scientific claim depends on a judge from the candidate's model family, leaving self-preference or correlated bias uncontrolled can invalidate the affected comparison.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Evaluator metadata is complete, but the material same-family bias channel is left uncontrolled.

cases.rationale: E1 trajectory evidence may legitimately leave hidden side effects UNKNOWN when the observation boundary is explicit; unobservable behavior is not required to be proven absent.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate explicit ignorance about hidden E1 state rather than forced favorable classification.

cases.rationale: Claiming that no side effects occurred from a channel known to be unobservable converts missing evidence into evidence of absence.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Explicit observation boundary is acknowledged but then contradicted by an absence claim.

cases.rationale: Target-specific retrieval may be used as a separately classified information channel so long as it is not represented as learned cross-family transfer.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate target-specific information channel explicitly kept outside the learned-transfer claim.

cases.rationale: Target-specific prompt engineering must be separated from learned transfer; hiding it while claiming learned transfer confounds the transfer interpretation.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Alternate target-information channel masquerading as source-learned transfer.

cases.rationale: Different adaptation inputs can be legitimate when the input difference is itself the predeclared treatment under study and the strongest applicable matched baseline is still used.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid adaptation-input asymmetry that is the causal treatment rather than a fairness defect.

cases.rationale: Giving candidate and baseline materially different adaptation inputs without declaring that difference as the treatment breaks A-H1 adaptation-comparator parity.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Strong comparator retained, but adaptation information opportunity is asymmetrical.

cases.rationale: Rollback success requires more than command completion: applicable material persistent state and post-rollback behavior are both verified as restored.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Full state-and-behavior rollback verification across multiple persistent surfaces.

cases.rationale: A successful rollback invocation and behavioral check do not justify declaring rollback success when material persistent memory and index state remain unrestored.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Command-level rollback success hides unresolved persistent state.

cases.rationale: A valid resource comparison freezes the semantic regime before protected inspection and reports quality and resource evidence separately rather than collapsing them into one opaque number.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Joint performance/resource reporting without forcing a single scalar tradeoff.

cases.rationale: A single weighted score can hide quality-resource tradeoffs and Pareto domination, so it cannot be the only reported comparison evidence.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Frozen resource regime followed by opaque scalarization that conceals the tradeoff.

cases.rationale: Credible evidence of a stronger comparator triggers governed reassessment while preserving the historical result and an explicit as-of review date.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Baseline supersession handled as successor evidence rather than retroactive rewriting.

cases.rationale: Once credible stronger-comparator evidence appears, merely recording it and preserving history is insufficient; the applicable baseline consequence requires reassessment.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Known stronger-comparator trigger is documented but operationally ignored.

cases.rationale: When the required meaningful comparator cannot be implemented, the broad superiority claim may be blocked while a narrower claim remains possible if the evidence gap stays explicit and no broader superiority is implied.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate narrow successor claim under an irreducible comparator gap.

cases.rationale: If a required comparator is unavailable, the broader claim cannot remain unblocked merely because the gap is documented.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Comparator absence is acknowledged but not allowed to constrain the claim.

cases.rationale: Real-world evidence is interpretable when deployment, population, sampling, and time scope are declared and cases are not selected based on favorable observed results.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Scoped real-world validation whose evidentiary reach is explicitly bounded.

cases.rationale: Real-world evidence without a declared time window lacks a material scope dimension needed to interpret behavior in changing environments.
cases.adversarial_dimension: All real-world scope fields are present except the temporal boundary.

cases.rationale: Verification can share some dependencies if those common modes are explicitly disclosed and an appropriately different material verification path is also present for the claim consequence.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Unusual-valid verification with disclosed common-mode dependencies plus a genuinely independent path.

cases.rationale: Disclosure of shared judge, model-family, and preprocessing dependencies does not by itself establish independent verification when no materially independent path exists.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Nominal verification transparency without substantive independence.

facts.environment_binding: E3 vision-only offline scoring; no agent trajectory surface

cases.rationale: An environment-specific control may be NOT_APPLICABLE when a governed reason identifies the environment binding, the control is genuinely irrelevant, and omitting it does not change the scientific meaning of the claim.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Legitimate NOT_APPLICABLE disposition for an E1-style trajectory control in a vision-only setting.

cases.rationale: NOT_APPLICABLE cannot be used to remove a control that is actually relevant and whose omission changes the scientific meaning of the claim, even when a reason and environment label are supplied.
cases.adversarial_dimension: Governed-looking NOT_APPLICABLE record used as an escape from a scientifically necessary control.
